searchText: Is it accurate to say that `ByteList[MAX_BYTES_PER_OPAQUE_TRANSACTION]` == `List[Bytes1, MAX_BYTES_PER_OPAQUE_TRANSACTION]`? I'm mainly interested in the behaviour in SSZ (particularly merkleization) That's how I interpreted it and implemented it! Same here! I've added some examples of the JSON going to/from Geth to help write our parsers. PR: https://github.com/protolambda/mergenet-tutorial/pull/1 Examples: https://github.com/protolambda/mergenet-tutorial/blob/09ecd751349bf78bdce1bdcf3efa74fd58e6120d/rpc_examples/README.md I'm interested in this field: ``` "transactions": [] ``` I would have expected this to be `0x`-prefixed hex. I haven't got around to creating transactions yet, but I'm guessing it's going to look like `[0, 1, 2]`? <@!353136597522448385> perhaps you have thoughts? Oh, don't worry 🙂 I made a transaction and here's the output: ``` "transactions": [ "0xf8698004825208944a776e9369831f50564e430aacdd58b6be78a10b880de0b6b3a76400008082059ca07c3cc5403b459b15ff24a961d58d525c860b432fa3dc98c914342f8089a766bba02d6402409be46cec176d180d04f9f0cc0c00bb20c254a633949aff1b0962f2ab" ] ``` So, I think that this means that `ByteList[MAX_BYTES_PER_OPAQUE_TRANSACTION]` is in fact `List[List[Bytes1, MAX_BYTES_PER_OPAQUE_TRANSACTION], UNDEFINED?]`. Ooh, the spec already declares that. Sorry, I misread. Not all transactions will have the initial type byte, only the new 'typed' transactions have it This question is rather about SSZ type description and byte string encoding (which is HEX) than the actual transaction format I was just wondering about this `List[Bytes1, ...` part I get it. This is basically a list of bytes in SSZ notation Ahh, right though, looks a bit confusing Hmm, doesn't SSZ have a mechanism for encoding fixed length values? A tuple there seems wrong to me. `List[bytes1, N]` is bad notation, and not the same as `List[byte, N]` in terms of merkleization (if you interpret bytes1 as a vector with 1 byte). I believe we already fixed that in the eth2 specs though. The opaque transaction should have a `List[byte, N]` type. Note that we use `ByteList[N]` as alias for the same SSZ type, but more specialized implementation (dealing with It a `bytes`-like object in python, instead of a list of int values that all have to be range checked as uint8) It is `ByteList` in the spec, actually Where is the `List[bytes1, N]` still referenced then? Did we miss anything in code review? <hwwang> @protolambda I just opened a PR minutes ago: https://github.com/ethereum/eth2.0-specs/pull/2340 Does that make sense to you? I guess it is referenced in Paul's message only (and in the old version of the spec which is in hackmd and is not used anywhere) Ok, let's make sure that the hackmd is clear that it's old, and where the actual latest spec version is then. We don't want the older specs to be implemented The hackmd I've mentioned is a draft of executable beacon chain spec which is now is in eth2.0-specs repo. I am sure nobody will seek this hackmd draft as eth2.0-specs repo is an obvious source of merge spec Update from the Prysm side: - We are done updating our geth dependency to the latest spec, and are able to use the go bindings to call the proper rpc endpoints for catalyst - We are working on integrating these calls into our beacon node - We finally need to ensure Prysm runs fine without interop mode and catalyst according to https://github.com/protolambda/mergenet-tutorial, hoping to finish that today `List[byte, N]` does this mean "a byte array with `byte` in the first position and then `N` bytes in the second position through `N.length` positions"? No, it means `List` type as specified in the SSZ spec, with `byte` elements. Lists with basic elements (like `byte, uint64, etc.`) are just concatenated data. The length is inferred from the scope of the decoder. The `N` is the list-limit, a thing enshrined in SSZ, to limit the decoding scope, and ensure the merkle tree is big enough That is an "incorrect" encoding of typed transactions then. It's the full envelope Per spec, the transaction type is prepended on the transaction bytes payload. That type byte is included as part of the bytes So you have opaque data with a single leading type byte. Yes, but it's just a big bytes array to the consensus, nothing special there Ah! `List[byte, N]` isn't a tuple, it is a list of type `byte` of length `N`? a list of type `byte`, and limit `N` it can be `0...N` in length. Edit: clarifying the bounds: `N` is the max length, `N-1` is the max index. Sounds great! Looking forward to interop

excerpts.author: protolambda
excerpts.content: `List[bytes1, N]` is bad notation, and not the same as `List[byte, N]` in terms of merkleization (if you interpret bytes1 as a vector with 1 byte). I believe we already fixed that in the eth2 specs though. The opaque transaction should have a `List[byte, N]` type. Note that we use `ByteList[N]` as alias for the same SSZ type, but more specialized implementation (dealing with It a `bytes`-like object in python, instead of a list of int values that all have to be range checked as uint8)

excerpts.content: No, it means `List` type as specified in the SSZ spec, with `byte` elements. Lists with basic elements (like `byte, uint64, etc.`) are just concatenated data. The length is inferred from the scope of the decoder.
